method: Complete plaintext source review, cleave facts (including literals and flow), atomscan before/after, five isolated Python source traces with effectful dependencies stubbed, and shared-rule controls outside test-directory exclusions.

source.scope: Primary report independently corroborates the configured component.zip URL, LOCALAPPDATA/Radmin staging, FamItrfc.exe --runtimechk action, RadminComponentRuntime task, three-hour recurrence and loader cleanup. This associates the scripts with the documented delivery chain; it does not establish that these scripts are original native CROSSROAD executables.

behavior: Both download an HTTPS ZIP without a pinned digest or signature check, extract it to LOCALAPPDATA/Radmin, and schedule FamItrfc.exe --runtimechk every three hours with schtasks /create /tr ... /sc HOURLY /mo 3 /f.
The scheduled executable is constructed from the same destination used for extraction. Its presence in the fetched ZIP is not checked. Neither script immediately executes it or runs schtasks /run.

Python runs only under the __main__ guard, creates the destination, uses TemporaryDirectory and ZipFile contexts, cleans temporary data before task creation, launches the command with shell=True/check=True, and unlinks __file__ only after task success. Five stubbed traces covered success, download/extraction/task failure, and unlink failure.

PowerShell executes at script top level with ErrorActionPreference=Stop, overwrites directory/archive extraction targets using -Force, checks LASTEXITCODE and throws on task failure, then deletes the downloaded archive and its PSCommandPath. There is no finally block to force cleanup on failure.

No obfuscation or encoded executable layer exists. Quoting/backticks escape the task action; they are not concealed code. No credential theft, exfiltration, direct command channel, privilege escalation or security-control bypass is present in either source.
verdict_basis: MALICIOUS for both: reachable acquisition from the independently documented hostile staging URL feeds the matching persistent executable action, followed by source cleanup. That specific configuration and executable chain tip the balance beyond ordinary installer capabilities. Deployment authorization, original registry package identity, author, signer and actual downstream bytes are unavailable; a research reproduction cannot be excluded.

payload_recovery.result: Failed after retries: DNS no such host. No payload was synthesized. Neither supplied script contains archive members; the remote ZIP and its members remain unverified.

trait_changes.reason: Action and overwrite flags do not establish unwanted persistence. Both the preexisting digest-verified maintenance setup and a command-string/shell=True equivalent matched at hostile severity before correction. All original required evidence, scope and confidence remain.

Bare referenced filenames establish neither that the containing artifact is Radmin nor that any signature is valid. Matcher, confidence, notable severity, types, Windows scope and inherited 1..5000000 byte bounds are preserved. The taxonomy now states the existing basename-reference boundary explicitly.

consumer_audit.forced_task: No exact-ID YAML consumers; scheduled-task ancestor remains unchanged and the finding remains suspicious.
consumer_audit.radmin: No exact-ID consumers. Reviewed twelve ancestor suppressor sites in ten YAML files, including CLR hosting, clipboard capture, Safe Mode, debugger/hook loading, module loading, RAT, reverse shell, account/log control, and UAC bypass. These require product identity for benign context: a filename reference must no longer trigger their remote-admin suppressor. Genuine Radmin identity rules remain unchanged; adding the moved reference back to suppressors would perpetuate the unsupported identity claim.
consumer_audit.destination: No basename-directory selector consumers. Five broader fs selectors in autorun/profile rules were inspected; none assert Radmin identity. Before/after controls showed no derived changes beyond the intended relocation.
consumer_audit.placement: Audited the executable-path catalog after encountering its 100-rule boundary. The moved matcher requires only a bare filename, matching the established basename home used for msedge.exe and firefox.exe, rather than any enclosing executable path. No catalog rule was removed or split to create capacity.

validation_before_final_gate.new_check: python3 testdata/triage/archive-task-second-review/check.py: five controls passed (verified argv installer, verified shell installer, two filename positives and one filename near miss).
validation_before_final_gate.outside_batch: All findings identical for task-stub.c, clickfix-update-stager.ps1, ps-cradle-stager.ps1 and setup-verified-library-download/setup.py. The existing maintenance PowerShell fixture was also unchanged. The two Python maintenance controls retained all findings with only forced-task hostile -> suspicious.
validation_before_final_gate.source_execution: Five Python traces passed without network, filesystem, archive or subprocess effects. PowerShell was statically traced; pwsh is unavailable.

coverage: Both retain a hostile CROSSROAD-associated chain finding and distinct suspicious self-deletion and repeating-task findings. No unsupported second hostile behavior was invented; generic downloading, extraction and process creation remain notable.
limits: Cleave reports flow-query-incomplete on Python; manual source tracing and isolated source execution resolve the relevant paths independently.
Atomscan v18.18 warns that the extractor emits v19 features; this model/schema mismatch may affect calibration.
PowerShell remains below the configured ML detection threshold despite a hostile rule finding; this is a classifier disagreement, not evidence of benign intent.
